summary_hint: who the landlord is, the rental property and tenant, the monthly rent, the lease start, and the late-payment count — so a processor can evaluate the borrower's housing-payment history and confirm an independent, arm's-length verifier without opening the form

typed_core.name: document_title
typed_core.why: identity — confirms this is a VOR

typed_core.name: landlord_or_property_manager_name
typed_core.why: identity — the certifying source

typed_core.name: landlord_contact_phone
typed_core.why: processor — landlord callback for follow-up (flattened from landlord_contact_information object)

typed_core.name: landlord_relationship_to_borrower
typed_core.why: disambiguator — arm's-length vs a relative-landlord; independence is meaningless without it
typed_core.prompt_hint: A related-party landlord (family member) undermines the VOR; capture the relationship even when it is only implied by a shared surname or address

typed_core.name: tenant_name
typed_core.why: identity — the borrower/tenant (flattened from person[])

typed_core.name: tenant_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — co-tenant when present (flattened)

typed_core.name: rental_property_address
typed_core.why: identity — which property the tenancy covers (degraded from address)

typed_core.name: lease_start_date
typed_core.why: processor — establishes the 12-month history window

typed_core.name: lease_end_date
typed_core.why: processor — remaining term / whether tenancy is ending

typed_core.name: current_tenant_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — is the borrower still the tenant (degraded from boolean)
typed_core.prompt_hint: 'Current tenant' vs a move-out date distinguishes an ongoing tenancy from a prior one — read this explicitly

typed_core.name: monthly_rent
typed_core.why: processor — headline rent; payment-shock and rental-history context

typed_core.name: rent_due_day
typed_core.why: processor — the due day used to judge lateness

typed_core.name: subsidy_or_concession
typed_core.why: disambiguator — a subsidy/concession changes the effective rent beside monthly_rent (flattened from object)

typed_core.name: late_payment_count
typed_core.why: processor — number of late rent payments (0x30 rental history)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Rental-history convention: '0x30' = zero payments 30+ days late in the window; the target is the late count, not prose

typed_core.name: returned_payment_count
typed_core.why: processor — NSF/returned rent payments

typed_core.name: current_arrears
typed_core.why: processor — amount currently past due

typed_core.name: eviction_or_collection_status
typed_core.why: processor — an eviction/collection is a material adverse signal (degraded from enum)

typed_core.name: verifier_name_title
typed_core.why: processor — who certified and their title (authority)

typed_core.name: verification_date
typed_core.why: identity/recency — certification date

typed_core.name: independent_source_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — whether the verifier is an independent/arm's-length source (degraded from boolean)

nested_lists.name: rent_payment_history
nested_lists.shape_reason: monthly rent history genuinely repeats and a VOR commonly spans 12-24 months, so flat rows keep it under the 16,384 ceiling

fields.name: month
fields.why: the payment month for the row

fields.name: payment_status
fields.why: on-time / late / returned status for the row (housing-payment performance)

fields.name: source
fields.why: the source of the row's data

rejected.name: form_number / form_revision_date
rejected.reason: VOR templates vary; no standardized-form consumer

rejected.name: statement_period_start / statement_period_end
rejected.reason: a VOR is a certification, not a statement period

rejected.name: loan_number / account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: not core to a VOR; catch-all captures if present

rejected.name: security_deposit
rejected.reason: OPTIONAL; no consumer for rental-history evaluation

rejected.name: signature_blocks / notary_block / document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: execution captured by verifier + independent_source_indicator; a VOR is not notarized

encoding_variations: Rent stated as gross vs net-of-concession — a '$1,800 (with $200 concession)' line means the effective rent is $1,600; always pair monthly_rent with subsidy_or_concession
Late history appears as a count ('2 late in 12 months'), a rating ('0x30'), or only in the month-by-month rows — read the explicit count and let the rows corroborate
Landlord relationship is the independence crux: 'professional property manager' vs 'borrower's father' carry very different weight — capture verbatim

open_questions.q: other_monthly_charges — second nested list. Utilities/parking/pet charges could matter for total housing cost.
options: (b) add a second flat list for other_monthly_charges
open_questions.recommendation: (a) keep only rent_payment_history now — no rule consumes ancillary charges yet, and monthly_rent + subsidy_or_concession carry the core figure

open_questions.q: eviction_or_collection_status enum degradation. Stored as free str; the value set is uncontrolled until a real corpus is seen.
open_questions.recommendation: keeping str; normalize in a future rule

notes: No rules read this document today (rule floor is empty). Fields are justified by identity, disambiguation, and processor use.
No SSN/account PII on a VOR. Tenant/landlord names are 'standard' sensitivity and stay in typed core for identity. Nothing needs _PII_FIELDS registration.
Budget is one nested list — other_monthly_charges is NOT nested (see open question 1).
